cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Merciful Lie
cards.instruction: Choose a truth your character believes would hurt someone. Keep it from them, even as honesty becomes harder.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's handle this professionally. The magazine hasn't rejected your poem. They think it deserves its own booklet.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They returned it. If even you think it's hopeless, I'll stop writing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can explain the standard again. Slowly. That's why they returned it. They can't give it enough space.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Will you write that on the cover? With your name?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Gladly. 'A voice that deserves more space.' Print my name large enough for the editor to see.

mechanism: A protects B from literary rejection by correcting B interpretation as a publishing-format issue and then controlling a public endorsement when B asks for one.
confusable: Selling a booklet alone lacks concealment of a painful truth; B explicit willingness to stop writing must motivate A reassurances.
comparison: Cake alternative blocks a tasting, while this alternative forces A to attach a name to the merciful fiction.
seedUse: Poem booklet and signed endorsement derive from D15-b; S03 contributes supposed publishing knowledge and precise correction of the cover wording.
